name: Scott Clem
residence: Campbell County (County 17: lifelong resident; family in the area for three generations)
occupation: Campbell County commissioner (appointed 2024; elected to a full term November 2026). County 17 reported prior work in social services, ministry, and public policy, including service as a Wyoming state representative.
education: Campbell County High School, 2002; associate's degree, Gillette College, 2005; bachelor's degree in theology, Liberty University (County 17, May 19, 2026). He attended the University of Wyoming for a year before a 2004 skiing accident.
prior_offices: Campbell County commissioner (appointed 2024; elected 2026). Wyoming House of Representatives, House District 31, 2015–2021 (County 17, May 19, 2026).
background: Scott Clem is a Campbell County commissioner. County 17 reported in May 2026 that he is a lifelong county resident whose family has been in the area for three generations, that he attended Wagon Wheel and Conestoga elementary schools and Sage Valley Junior High, graduated from Campbell County High School in 2002, attended the University of Wyoming for a year, was paralyzed in a skiing accident in 2004, earned an associate's degree from Gillette College in 2005 and a bachelor's degree in theology from Liberty University, and has worked in social services, ministry, and public policy. The paper reported that he served in the Wyoming Legislature from 2015 to 2021, representing Gillette and Campbell County, and was appointed to the county commission in 2024 to fill an open seat. He won a full term in the November 3, 2026, general election.
